content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"no","applies_why":"The judge does not ground UNDERDETERMINED on a single verse failing to state a link or its contrary; it grounds it on the challenger pressing a limb the defender had dropped.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"the phrase \"single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground\" weighed against the judge's \"no live link remains to contradict\": reading 1, the rule bars only using a verse's silence as the ground; reading 2, it also bars using the absence of a live contradiction after a dropped limb.","why":"The judge's stated reason is the dropped limb and absence of a live link to contradict, not that a single verse fails to state a link or its contrary."}
